minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued the after-the-fact farm field filing to June 5 and approved several smaller permits.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a run of wetlands hearings. It closed out a house, two deck/wall requests and a lake-side deck, and continued three matters, including a contested after-the-fact farm clearing with neighbor complaints. It also discussed a boulder-marker dispute at a subdivision, a land purchase update and a homeowner outreach pamphlet.

public_comment.topic: Abutter near 389 Pasty Street worried about water supply, night-time work, strobe lights and equipment damage from the farm field.
Neighbor worried the clearing happened first, well going dry, soil, fertilizer runoff, lights and cracked driveway.
Neighbor on shared driveway concerned about damage to the driveway and wells going dry, asks about recourse.

suggested_reports.title: Conservation land encroachments
suggested_reports.question: How often does clearing or building in wetland buffers happen without a filing, and how is it handled?

what_happened.line: The commission continued the after-the-fact farm field filing at 389 Pasty Street to June 5 after neighbors raised concerns about wells and lighting.
The agent is to review the farm plan with the conservation service, add a well component and make a site visit before the June 5 return.
A negative determination for the retaining wall at 251 Prospect Street passed, and the 205 Sunset Lane request was continued to June 19.
The 14 Sunset Avenue notice of intent was continued, with updated drawings showing buffer-zone square footage due five days before the next hearing.
A dispute over boulder markers at a subdivision was not resolved; the agent will research the original orders for whether boulders were required.

why_it_matters: Neighbors of the 389 Pasty Street field raised well-water, runoff and driveway-damage concerns, and the continued hearing is where those questions can be weighed before any approval of the already-cleared land.
Land purchases without a budgeted line depend on trust-fund transfers and purchase orders, so such acquisitions can proceed outside the regular budget vote.
watch_next: June 5 continued hearing on the 389 Pasty Street agricultural conversion, with the agent's farm plan review and site visit.
June 19 continued request for determination at 205 Sunset Lane.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on most hearings and continuances, though ours leaves many vote outcomes as "not audible" where the official gives unanimous votes. The key difference to check is the 14 Sunset Ave continuance (June 15 in ours, June 5 officially). Also check the pamphlet, which ours treats as still under review and the official says was approved, and whether Richard Bursch arrived late or was absent.
